messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT PAGER (sev-1) — detected spike in GPU interconnect errors in us-east-1. Error rate > 12% over last 5m, multiple host kernel logs showing mlx5/PCIe link flaps. Pager to @Lee (oncall).

Lee (oncall): Ack. I'm on it. pulling dashboards now. can someone post the alert link? :eyes:

Jordan (sre): Alert: https://prom.redwood.internal/alerts/1998456789 — shows packet drops on nic_rx_errors and a correlated bump in inference tail latency. Top affected pool: gpu-pool-us-east-a.

Anya (infra): I'm seeing NIC firmware messages on two hosts (host-1432, host-1439) that match a known interconnect regression with certain AWS Nitro versions. Kernel dmesg extracts below.

Anya (infra): ```
[Jun 10 03:12:14] mlx5_core 0000:06:00.0: mlx5_core: NIC link down (err -5)
[Jun 10 03:12:14] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Corrected error received: status 0x00001000
[Jun 10 03:12:15] nv_peer_mem: REMOTE ACCESS ERROR: nvlink handshake failed
```

Devin (runtime): Noted. We're seeing 500ms+ p50->p95 token latencies for active model routes hitting those hosts. KV cache misses spike when nodes flapped, causing backpressure. Rolling model fallback to cheaper variant would help short-term.

Lee (oncall): Quick mitigation: cordon host-1432 and host-1439 from scheduler and drain non-critical jobs. Can someone run `kubectl cordon` + `drain`? I'll trigger traffic routing to fallback pool.

Tim (ops): I'm on cordon/drain for host-1432. Running: `kubectl drain gpu-node-1432 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -w`. 20 pods draining, two reraise due to stuck volumes, working on those.

Jordan (sre): Adding a runbook note: when interconnect link flaps cause KV invalidations, we see cascade of cache misses; mitigation is: 1) cordon; 2) scale fallback; 3) bump routing weight away from region if >40% hosts impacted.

Alex (cs): Heads up — customers in us-east-1 may see 502/504 for streaming responses. I'm pre-emptively messaging a short status note to affected accounts (low volume customers) and adding to status page if we need.

Devin (runtime): Temporarily increasing autoscale for fallback-pool by +30% to absorb drained capacity. Executing: `redwoodctl pool scale fallback-pool-us-east --delta 30`

Maria (platform): I see a cloud provider incident advisory referencing an interconnect firmware push in us-east-1 around 02:50 UTC. Link: https://status.aws.example/incident/xyz (internal copy attached). They report transient NIC resets for a subset of Nitro instances.

Jin (ml): Any customer-facing model quality regressions? If we're switching model variants, we should tag eval traces for postmortem comparison.

Devin (runtime): Good call. Enabling evaluation tagging for all requests routed to fallback variants: `featureflag enable eval-tagging/fallback-1998456789`

Lee (oncall): Host-1439 drain started. Observability shows tail latency improving on routes once traffic shifts. We'll keep cordoned hosts offline and open a support ticket with AWS.

Anya (infra): Opening support case with AWS. Case ID: 1234567890. Providing kernel logs and PCIe AER counters. Requested escalation to NIC firmware team.

Jordan (sre): Timeline so far:
- 02:47 UTC — small spike in p95 latency, minor error counts
- 02:50 UTC — AWS reported interconnect firmware push in region
- 03:11 UTC — alert threshold breached, incident-bot paged oncall
- 03:12 UTC — kernel AER and mlx5 messages observed on host-1432/1439
- 03:15 UTC — hosts cordoned and draining, traffic shifted to fallback pool
- 03:25 UTC — p95 tail latency trending down, error rate falling to baseline
(keeping monitoring open)

Lee (oncall): Can we get a log bundle for the impacted hosts and API gateway logs for the affected time window (02:40-03:30)? I'll attach to the RCA thread.

Tim (ops): Uploading bundles to S3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/1998456789/host-1432-dmesg.log and host-1439-dmesg.log. Also gw-logs: s3://redwood-incident-logs/1998456789/gateway-02-40-03-30.log

Devin (runtime): Noticed a secondary symptom: model instance eviction rate increased for routes pinned to those hosts (OOM killer not implicated). Could be NV peer mem timeouts causing runtime crashes. Stack trace snippet attached:```
2026-06-10T03:12:15Z runtime ERROR: nv_peer_mem:recv timeout, session closed
2026-06-10T03:12:15Z runtime WARN: kvcache invalidation, id=0x7f3b1
```

Jin (ml): We'll mark eval sets impacted between 03:10-03:30 and run regression checks against baseline. Please tag traces with `incident:1998456789`.

Alex (cs): Notifying three paying customers who reported elevated latency at 03:20. Messaging draft: "We detected transient GPU interconnect issues in us-east-1 between 02:50–03:25 UTC; we've shifted your workloads and do not expect data exposure. We're investigating root cause and will follow up." Want review before send.

Lee (oncall): Draft looks good. Send, and cc SRE + CS.

Anya (infra): AWS replied: they saw increased AER counts for Nitro instances with certain NIC firmware, they've scheduled a rollback/mitigation and recommend avoiding affected instance family until fix. Attach: vendor debug bundle link.

Jordan (sre): Hypotheses to track in RCA thread: 1) AWS NIC firmware regression causing corrected AER/PCIe resets -> host-level NVPN/NVLink handshake failures -> KV cache invalidations -> tail latency. 2) Scheduling pressure during drain exacerbated latency due to cold-starts for model instances. 3) Rare simultaneous kernel AER + driver bug causing process restarts.

Devin (runtime): Evidence: dmesg AER + runtime nv_peer_mem timeouts + sudden KV cache miss spike. Counter-evidence: no OOMs, no persistent host hardware ECC counts. Suggest primary hypothesis = interconnect firmware regression.

Lee (oncall): Short term mitigation checklist (in-thread):
- cordon/drain affected hosts (done)
- scale fallback pools (done)
- tag traces/evals (done)
- notify customers (in progress)
- open cloud support case (done)

Tim (ops): All done. I left the hosts cordoned but not rebooted. Recommend we avoid reboot until vendor confirms root cause to preserve logs.

Anya (infra): Agree. Preserving logs is critical. We'll snapshot disks and capture full kernel logs.

Jordan (sre): Post-incident action items (to be tracked):
- Add automated detection for nv_peer_mem timeouts correlated with AER counts.
- Document runbook step to scale fallback pool automagically when >5% hosts in pool report AER.
- Add guidance for AWS instance family avoidance until vendor fix.

Jin (ml): I'll collate evaluation diffs and surface any quality regressions. If customers see generation divergence, we'll correlate with the eval tags.

Alex (cs): Sending customer messages now. I'll post copy in #status-updates for transparency.

Lee (oncall): De-escalating pager as error rate is down to 1.2%. Keeping incident as open for RCA. We'll reconvene for postmortem in 24h. Thanks all. :handshake:

incident-bot: Incident updated: status -> mitigated. RCA channel will be created: #incidents-1998456789-rca

Lee (oncall): Adding action: please upload any additional logs to the S3 incident path and add findings to the RCA channel. Closing live coordination thread.
